title: Conventional commit type must be in the enum
summary: The commit type must be one of build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test; anything else (e.g. 'foo: some message') is not a conventional commit.

source.rule: type-enum (error, always)
if (!types.some((type) => new RegExp(`^${type}$`).test(result.type))) { raiseError(`Unknown release type "${result.type}" found in pull request title "${prTitle}".`) }
types: | fix / feat / JIRA-\d+ — Configure which types are allowed (newline-delimited). These are regex patterns auto-wrapped in `^ $`.

tests.label: non-enum type fails
tests.input: foo: some message

tests.label: enum type passes
tests.input: fix: some message

notes: type-enum restricts to the Angular-derived list while the specification allows any type; match on the header only, with optional scope and optional '!'.

title: Commit type must be lower-case
summary: Types like 'FIX: some message' break conventional-commit parsing and tooling; the type must be lower-case.

source.rule: type-case (error, always, lower-case)
module.exports = { extends: ["@commitlint/config-conventional"], helpUrl: "https://www.conventionalcommits.org/", ignores: [(msg) => /Signed-off-by: dependabot\[bot]/m.test(msg)] }

tests.label: upper-case type fails
tests.input: FIX: some message

tests.label: lower-case type passes
tests.input: fix: some message

notes: Also covers type-empty ('': some message fails); the type must be present and lower-case.

title: Subject is required
summary: A commit like 'fix:' with no subject after the colon carries no information; the subject must be non-empty.

source.rule: subject-empty (error, never)
if (!result.subject) { raiseError(`No subject found in pull request title "${prTitle}".`) }

tests.label: missing subject fails
tests.input: fix:

tests.label: subject present passes
tests.input: fix: some message

notes: Subject length is bounded separately by header-max-length (ZS-COMMIT-005).

title: Subject must not be sentence/start/pascal/upper-case
summary: Subjects like 'Some Message' or 'SomeMessage' are a stylistic tell; use a plain lower-case subject ('some message').

source.rule: subject-case (error, never, [sentence-case, start-case, pascal-case, upper-case])
subjectPattern: ^(?![A-Z]).+$ — This example ensures the subject doesn't start with an uppercase character.

tests.label: sentence-case subject fails
tests.input: fix(scope): Some message

tests.label: lower-case subject passes
tests.input: fix(scope): some message

notes: Lower-case subject is preferred; the case restriction applies to the first word of the subject.

title: Header max length (100)
summary: Headers over 100 characters break readability in git tooling; the whole header (type + scope + subject) must stay within one line of 100 chars.

source.rule: header-max-length (error, always, 100)

tests.label: overlong header fails
tests.input: fix: some message that is way too long and breaks the line max-length by several characters while still being a realistic commit header

tests.label: short header passes
tests.input: fix: some message

notes: Also implies header-trim: no leading/trailing whitespace on the header line.

title: Blank line before body and footer
summary: The body and footer must be separated from the header by a blank line, or git tooling cannot distinguish them from the subject.

source.rule: body-leading-blank (warning, always)
footer-leading-blank (warning, always)

tests.label: body glued to header fails
tests.input:
fix: some message
body

tests.label: blank line present passes
tests.input:
fix: some message

body

notes: Warning tier in commitlint (non-blocking by default) and mapped to warning here to stay faithful to the source.

title: Body/footer lines max 100 chars
summary: Each body and footer line over 100 characters breaks readability in git tooling; URL-containing lines are exempt.

source.rule: body-max-line-length (error, always, 100)
footer-max-line-length (error, always, 100)

tests.label: long body line fails
tests.input:
fix: some message

body with multiple lines
has a message that is way too long and will break the line rule 'line-max-length' by several characters

tests.label: short body lines pass
tests.input:
fix: some message

body with multiple lines
but still no line is too long

notes: Lines containing URLs are exempt per commitlint.

title: All PR commits must be conventional
summary: Every commit in a PR must match the Conventional Commits format (`type: description`, `type(scope): description`, `type(scope)!: description`), not just the PR title.

source.rule: require-conventional-commits (default false)
CONVENTIONAL_PATTERN /^\w+(?:\([^)]+\))?!?:\s.+/
If the config file doesn't exist, config-conventional settings will be loaded as a default fallback. (the action lints every commit of the pull request, not only the head commit)

tests.input: feat(auth): add refresh token rotation

notes: The implementation accepts any `\w+` type; PR titles with a trailing '(#123)' are tolerated.

title: Commit message max length (500)
summary: Individual commit messages over 500 characters are flagged; overly long messages are a sign of unreviewed, unscoped changes.

source.rule: max-commit-message-length (default 500)

title: Commit author must match PR author
summary: Every commit in the PR must be authored by the same GitHub user who opened the PR; mismatched authors indicate squashed or hijacked contributions.

source.rule: require-commit-author-match (default true)

summary: Commits authored by blocked usernames (e.g. known spam/AI-slop accounts) fail the PR; the blocklist is repository-configured.

source.rule: blocked-commit-authors (default empty)

title: Emoji cap in PR title and description (2)
summary: More than 2 emojis in the PR title and description combined is a slop signal; emoji decorate rather than communicate.

source.rule: max-emoji-count (default 2)
max-emoji-count: Maximum number of emojis allowed in the PR title and description. 0 disables this check. Default: 2

tests.label: 3 emojis fails
tests.input: feat: add export 🚀✨🔥 (title + description combined)

tests.label: one emoji passes
tests.input: fix: correct the timezone offset 🕐

title: Linked issue required in PR description
summary: PRs must reference at least one issue; unreferenced PRs cannot be traced to the work they fix.

source.rule: require-linked-issue (default false)

tests.label: no issue reference fails
tests.input: Adds export button to the dashboard.

tests.label: issue reference passes
tests.input: Closes #123: adds export button to the dashboard.

notes: Requires the PR to reference at least one issue in the description; default is opt-in.

title: PR template required
summary: When enabled, the PR description must follow the repository's PR template structure (strict sections with all checkboxes present and checked); template-less AI-slop PRs are caught.

source.rule: require-pr-template (default false)

tests.label: template sections missing fails
tests.input: PR description lacks the repo template's 'What changed?' and 'Testing' sections

tests.label: template followed passes
tests.input: PR description contains all template sections with checkboxes checked

notes: strict-pr-template-sections must be present and checked; optional-pr-template-sections may be removed; extra sections beyond max-additional-pr-template-sections fail.

title: Doc-only spam paths blocked (README/LICENSE/SECURITY/CODE_OF_CONDUCT)
summary: PRs that only touch README.md, SECURITY.md, LICENSE, or CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md are the classic slop-spam pattern (fake contributions with no real code); those paths are blocked by default.

source.rule: blocked-paths (default README.md, SECURITY.md, LICENSE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

tests.label: README-only PR fails
tests.input: PR changes: README.md (adds 'Sponsor' link)

tests.label: code PR passes
tests.input: PR changes: src/auth/refresh.ts + its test

notes: Blocked paths are repository-configurable; entries ending in '/' match folders. Genuine doc updates should accompany code or be routed through the maintainers' process.

title: Changed files must end with a newline
summary: Every changed file must end with a newline character; missing final newlines are a mechanical hygiene failure and a sign of un-reviewed generation.

source.rule: require-final-newline (default true)

tests.label: file without final newline fails
tests.input: const x = 1; // no trailing newline at EOF

tests.label: file with final newline passes
tests.input: const x = 1;

notes: Applies to all changed files in the PR; classic POSIX text-file convention.

title: Max changed files in a PR (50)
summary: PRs touching more than 50 files are unreviewable and typical of sweep-style AI slop PRs; split the work.

source.rule: max-changed-files (default 50)

tests.label: 51 changed files fails
tests.input: PR changes 51 files (additions+deletions across the repo)

tests.label: 12 changed files passes
tests.input: PR changes 12 files

notes: 0 disables the check. Complementary max-changed-lines (10000) guards mega-diffs in few files.

title: One logical change per commit
summary: Do not bundle multiple unrelated file changes into a single commit; each commit carries one descriptive message so history stays clean, revertable, and cherry-pickable.

source.rule: Git Commit Rules: create separate commits per file with descriptive messages
Each commit does one logical thing ... Separate refactoring from feature work. A refactoring change and a feature change are two different changes — submit them separately.
Prefer one commit per coherent change. If one diff contains unrelated release visible changes, recommend splitting it.

tests.label: bundled commit fails
tests.input: commit 'update stuff' touches README.md, src/service.ts, and a skill file together

tests.label: focused commit passes
tests.input: commit 'docs: explain subagent frontmatter' touches only the subagent doc file

notes: Consistency/hygiene lock: separate commits make git history cleaner, easier to review, revert, or cherry-pick individual changes.

title: Vague or informational commit subject
summary: Subjects like 'wip', 'minor fix', 'fix bug', 'phase 1', 'stuff', or 'misc changes' carry no information a future reader (or git bisect) can act on; a subject must say what actually changed.

source.rule: Change Descriptions: anti-patterns ('Fix bug,' 'Fix build,' 'Add patch,' 'Moving code from A to B,' 'Phase 1,' 'Add convenience functions.')
Anti-patterns: "Fix bug," "Fix build," "Add patch," "Moving code from A to B," "Phase 1," "Add convenience functions."
Avoid vague implementation notes like `add some feature`, `update stuff`, or `fix issue`. Prefer user-facing outcomes such as `support custom scopes`.

tests.label: vague subject fails
tests.input:
wip
fix: minor fix
chore: misc changes

tests.label: informative subject passes
tests.input:
fix: guard against null order total
feat(api): add refresh-token rotation

notes: Triage: conventional types like `refactor:` are fine; the term match targets the subject's filler wording, not the type prefix. A subject that names the changed thing passes even when short.

title: Gerund (non-imperative) commit subject
summary: A subject that starts with a gerund ('fix: updating the rpc client') describes what happened instead of commanding the change; the first line must be short, imperative, and standalone ('fix: update the rpc client').

source.rule: First line: Short, imperative, standalone. 'Delete the FizzBuzz RPC' not 'Deleting the FizzBuzz RPC.'
First line: Short, imperative, standalone. "Delete the FizzBuzz RPC" not "Deleting the FizzBuzz RPC."

tests.label: gerund subject fails
tests.input:
fix: updating the rpc client
docs: adding migration notes

tests.label: imperative subject passes
tests.input:
fix: update the rpc client
docs: add migration notes

notes: Only gerunds in the common AI/LLM subject set are matched to avoid adjective false positives ('pending', 'existing', 'streaming').

title: Change size cap (1000 added lines)
summary: A PR adding ~1000 lines is too large to review in one sitting; split it into focused changes (~100 lines is good, ~300 acceptable for a single logical change).

source.rule: Change Sizing: ~100 lines good, ~300 acceptable, ~1000 too large — split it
Target ~100 lines per commit/PR. Changes over ~1000 lines should be split. ~1000 lines → Split into smaller changes.

tests.label: 1200 added lines fails
tests.input: PR diff adds 1200 lines across 8 files

tests.label: 260 added lines passes
tests.input: PR diff adds 260 lines across 3 files

notes: Complementary to ZS-COMMIT-019 (changed-file count) and ZS-CODE-045 (single-file size). File deletions and mechanical refactors may exceed the cap with justification.

title: Bulk dependency bump without named packages
summary: A subject like 'bump deps' merges many upgrades nobody can review; one dependency per change with the package named ('bump lodash from 4.17.20 to 4.17.21') keeps the cause and the revert clean.

source.rule: One dependency per change; bulk 'bump deps' merges are the riskiest upgrades
One dependency per change. ... the riskiest upgrades are the ones merged in bulk with a message like "bump deps." A bulk bump that breaks the build hides which package did it.
For dependency-only work: Use `fix(deps)` for runtime dependency updates in `dependencies` when `deps` is an accepted scope. Use `dev-deps` for development-only tooling dependency updates.

tests.label: bulk bump fails
tests.input:
chore: bump deps
chore: update dependencies

tests.label: named single bump passes
tests.input: chore(deps): bump lodash from 4.17.20 to 4.17.21

notes: A bump that names the exact package and versions is a reviewable single change; a blanket 'bump deps' hides which package caused a breakage.

title: Mixed-concern commit subject (refactor + feature in one commit)
summary: A subject that both refactors and adds/fixes describes two changes, so the diff cannot be reviewed, reverted or understood as one unit — and review comments land on the wrong half. Refactors ship separately from behavior changes.

source.rule: Separate refactoring from feature work. A change that refactors existing code and adds new behavior is two changes — submit them separately.
Bad: Mixed concerns — git commit -m "refactor validation and add phone number field"
Don't combine formatting changes with behavior changes. Don't combine refactors with features. Each type of change should be a separate commit — and ideally a separate PR

tests.label: refactor-and-add subject fails
tests.input: refactor: rename validation helpers and add phone number validation

tests.label: pure refactor subject passes
tests.input: refactor: extract validation helpers into a shared module

notes: Header-only; requires a refactor-class verb joined by `and` to a feature-class verb (either order). Comma-separated laundry lists (`fix sidebar, update deps, refactor utils`) and two-feature subjects that do not involve a refactor verb are not matched — see ZS-COMMIT-020/021 for those.

title: Subject must not end with a full stop
summary: conventional-commit subjects are changelog bullets, so a trailing '.' is a tell of pasted prose; the period belongs in the body or in a closing footer ('Fixes #123.').

source.rule: subject-full-stop (condition: subject ends with value; rule: never; value '.') — echo "fix: some message." # fails
description is required immediately after ': '. Keep it concise, changelog-ready ... Do not end it with a period.

tests.label: subject ending in a period fails
tests.input: fix: some message.

tests.label: period in the body or footer passes
tests.input:
fix(cli): preserve the prerelease tag

Fixes #123.

notes: Header-scoped: a body sentence or a trailing footer period is untouched. Complements ZS-COMMIT-004 (subject case) and ZS-COMMIT-005 (length).

title: Scope must be lower-case
summary: A scope shouted as 'fix(SCOPE):' is rejected by the Angular config and by PR-title scope gates; scopes name a section of the codebase, so they stay lower-case ('fix(scope):').

source.rule: "scope-case": [2, "always", "lower-case"]
echo "fix(SCOPE): some message" # fails
disallowScopes: | release / [A-Z]+ — by setting the value below ... `ci(e2e,release): ...` will be rejected

tests.label: upper-case scope fails
tests.input: fix(SCOPE): some message

tests.label: lower-case and camelCase-free scopes pass
tests.input: fix(scope): some message

tests.label: scopeless header passes
tests.input: fix: some message

notes: Mirrors type-case (ZS-COMMIT-002) for the scope segment; a mixed-case scope such as fix(apiV2): also fails. config-conventional itself does not enable scope-case, config-angular does. config-angular's other extras are deliberately not ported: subject-exclamation-mark ('never') contradicts the conventional `!` marker ZS-COMMIT-001 accepts, and header-max-length 72 is a config choice, not a new tell (ZS-COMMIT-005 uses 100).

title: Commit header must not be padded with whitespace
summary: A header with leading or trailing whitespace lints green on length yet breaks in git log and grep output; commitlint's header-trim is an error-level rule in config-conventional.

source.rule: header-trim — condition: `header` must not have initial or trailing whitespaces
"header-trim": [RuleConfigSeverity.Error, "always"]

tests.label: trailing whitespace on the header fails
tests.input: fix: correct the retry count

tests.label: clean header passes
tests.input:
fix: correct the retry count

Body line.

notes: ZS-COMMIT-005's summary and the zeroslop-audit-commit checklist claim header-trim is implied by the 100-char cap, but its pattern (^.{101,}$) cannot catch a padded short header — this rule is the missing half, not a duplicate.

title: Unbackticked @-token pings a GitHub user
summary: A bare @-prefixed token (scoped package, decorator, JSDoc tag) is parsed by GitHub as a user mention, linking and notifying an unrelated account; wrap it in backticks.

source.rule: Wrap any `@`-prefixed token that is not an intentional GitHub user mention in backticks — scoped package names (`@types/node`), decorators (`@Injectable`), JSDoc/annotation tags (`@deprecated`). GitHub parses a bare `@name` in commit messages and changelogs as a user mention, which can link and notify an unrelated GitHub account.

tests.label: bare scoped package and doc tag fail
tests.input:
feat: add @types/node support to the loader

Bare @deprecated tags are no longer rewritten.

tests.label: backticked token and e-mail address pass
tests.input:
feat: add `@types/node` support to the loader

Backticked `@deprecated` tags keep working; mail still goes to ops@example.com.

notes: Pattern only fires on token shapes that are never intentional mentions (owner/repo scope, doc tags); a deliberate 'cc @reviewer' is untouched, and an @ preceded by a backtick or by a word character (e-mail) is not matched.

title: Breaking-change footer token must be upper-case
summary: Conventional Commit units are case-insensitive except one: release tooling only recognises the footer token as `BREAKING CHANGE` (or `BREAKING-CHANGE`), so 'breaking change:' silently drops the major bump.

source.rule: Conventional Commit units are not case-sensitive, except `BREAKING CHANGE`, which must be uppercase when used as that footer token.
Footer tokens use hyphens instead of spaces, such as `Reviewed-by`, except for `BREAKING CHANGE`. `BREAKING-CHANGE` is synonymous with `BREAKING CHANGE`.

tests.label: lower-case footer token fails
tests.input:
feat!: drop the legacy fallback

breaking change: token fallbacks are no longer applied.

tests.label: upper-case footer token passes
tests.input:
feat!: drop the legacy fallback

BREAKING CHANGE: token fallbacks are no longer applied.

tests.label: hyphenated upper-case synonym passes
tests.input:
feat!: drop the legacy fallback

BREAKING-CHANGE: token fallbacks are no longer applied.

notes: Case-sensitive on purpose so the canonical `BREAKING CHANGE:` never trips it; the realistic mixed casings (breaking change:, Breaking Change:) are matched.

title: Footer tokens use hyphens, not spaces
summary: A trailer written as 'Signed off by:' / 'Reviewed by:' is not a footer token at all — parsers, DCO bots and changelog tooling key on the hyphenated form ('Signed-off-by:').

source.rule: Footer tokens use hyphens instead of spaces, such as `Reviewed-by`, except for `BREAKING CHANGE`.

tests.label: space-separated trailer fails
tests.input:
docs: add the migration guide

Signed off by: Jane Doe <jane@example.com>

tests.label: hyphenated trailers pass
tests.input:
docs: add the migration guide

Signed-off-by: Jane Doe <jane@example.com>
Reviewed-by: Kim <kim@example.com>

notes: Case-sensitive so ordinary prose ('as suggested by the reviewer') is not flagged; the space-variant set is the hyphenated trailer vocabulary in its spaced spelling, and 'BREAKING CHANGE' is deliberately exempt (see the footer-case rule).

title: Passive-voice commit subject
summary: A subject that states what happened ('custom scopes were added') reads as a changelog of events; an active verb phrase ('support custom scopes') commands the change and stays imperative.

source.rule: Active verb phrases are usually better than passive sentences. Prefer `support custom scopes` over `custom scopes were added` unless passive voice is clearly more natural for the project.

tests.label: passive subject fails
tests.input: feat: custom scopes were added to the writer

tests.label: imperative subject passes
tests.input: feat: support custom scopes in the writer

tests.label: present-tense copula is not flagged
tests.input: fix: the flag is enabled by default

notes: Only past-tense auxiliaries (was/were/had been/has been/have been) trigger it, so descriptive 'is/are' subjects are not flagged; complementary to ZS-COMMIT-022 (gerund subjects), which catches a different non-imperative shape.

title: Emoji-only commit title has no description
summary: In gitmoji repos the emoji is the intention and a message is still required ('<intention> [scope?][:?] <message>'); a title made of emoji alone carries no information for humans or changelogs.

source.rule: `<intention> [scope?][:?] <message>` — `intention`: An emoji from the list. `scope`: An optional string ... `message`: A brief explanation of the change.
Commit your changes. Don't forget to add a commit title with an emoji and a description.

tests.label: emoji plus description passes
tests.input: ✨ add the deploy workflow

tests.label: conventional title without emoji passes
tests.input: feat: add the deploy workflow

tests.label: blank header is not this rule's business

notes: Flags the absence of a message, not the emoji (gitmoji repos legitimately lead with one); an emoji-only header also trips ZS-COMMIT-008, but this rule names the gitmoji-specific defect.

title: AI co-author trailer in commit message
summary: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` and `Generated with [Claude Code]` trailers record model provenance in permanent history; upstream's attribution rule covers the trailer form.

source.rule: no-ai-attribution pattern branch: co-?authored-by:\s*(?:claude|chatgpt|openai|anthropic|copilot|gemini)

tests.label: claude trailer fails
tests.input:
feat(api): add rate limiting to the public endpoints

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

tests.label: normal commit passes
tests.input:
feat(api): add rate limiting to the public endpoints

Instrumented with Prometheus counters; limits come from config.

notes: Commit-domain twin of the code-domain attribution rule (same upstream pattern). Scope limits the match to the trailer/generator strings; a human co-author or a scaffold script is untouched. Teams that require provenance disclosure should allowlist this rule instead of deleting it.
